items.followUp: Give two differences between fungi and animals.

rubric.why: Fungal cell walls contain chitin, whereas plant cell walls contain cellulose.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the cell-wall materials of fungi and plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fungal walls contain chitin and plant walls contain cellulose.

rubric.why: Fungi lack chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically, unlike plants that generally photosynthesize.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the mode of nutrition of fungi from that of plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fungi lack chlorophyll or do not photosynthesize and obtain food heterotrophically.

modelAnswer: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, while plant cell walls are made of cellulose.
Fungi lack chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically, while plants generally make food by photosynthesis.

items.followUp: What happens to the reaction rate when all enzyme active sites are occupied by substrate?

rubric.why: Saturation refers to all available enzyme active sites being involved.
rubric.description: States that all the enzyme's active sites are occupied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that every active site is occupied.

rubric.why: The active sites are occupied by substrate molecules in the saturated state.
rubric.description: Identifies substrate molecules as occupying the active sites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the active sites are occupied or filled by substrate.

modelAnswer: When all the enzyme's active sites are occupied by substrate molecules, the condition is called saturation of active sites.

items.followUp: State one use of enzymes in the textile industry.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used to remove ink from paper during recycling.
rubric.description: Identifies enzymatic de-inking of recycled paper.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes remove ink from paper.

rubric.why: Enzymes are also used to improve the quality of paper.
rubric.description: Gives another use of enzymes in the paper industry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes improve paper quality.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are used to remove ink from recycled paper (de-inking).
They are also used to improve the quality of paper.
